section: IV. Course Management
text: IV. Course Management 1. Academic Year and Class Schedules The academic year at MedTech consists of two terms: Fall (from September to December) and Spring (from January to May), and an optional summer term (from end May to end June). Each term stretches over 15 weeks except the summer session which stretches over five weeks only. Class meeting times are typically scheduled Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. Make-up classes may be scheduled on Saturdays, with at least a week’s notice from the professor or the administration. MedTech classes are held once, twice or three times a week. 2. Attendance and Audit Regular and prompt attendance in all class and laboratory sessions is compulsory and essential to successful teaching and learning. Faculty are required to maintain records of student attendance through the university’s course management system (CMS). The administration also assesses the attendance on a regular basis. section: V. Entrance Requirements to the Engineering
text: V. Entrance Requirements to the Engineering Program To be admitted to the engineering program, students must successfully complete the two-year foundational program common to all engineering specializations and meet the following requirements: ▪ Having a score > 12/20. The student's score is accounted for through: o 20% Baccalaureate o 40% Year 1 o 40% Year 2 ▪ Having no courses with a failing grade. Students are required to re-take all courses for which a failing grade was received. ▪ Not exceeding one (1) D+ per term ▪ Having a grade of C or above on 80 % of core engineering courses (Math, Physics, Chemistry, Electronics, Computer Science, English) ▪ Having completed a pre-engineering internship. ▪ Having at most one pre-engineering year retake Students must choose one of the following engineering programs offered by MedTech: Computer Systems Engineering, Software Engineering or Renewable Energy Engineering. The final acceptance into the requested program is decided by the committee taking into consideration many aspects such as student grades, capacity limits for the specific program and number of applicants. See section “Assessment and Grades” for details on letter grades.

Final exams will not be returned to students however they are welcome to schedule a time to view their exam for 5 minutes and return them back to the instructor during the appeal period. Some courses are assessed using a Pass/Fail grade. Others would assign a letter grade to each student at the end of the term reflecting the level of the student’s academic performance in that course. text: VIII. Academic Integrity and Code of Conduct 1. Integrity MedTech places a strong emphasis on the integrity of the academic work. It is the responsibility of all MedTech community members, including faculty, staff, and students, to conduct all academic endeavors with honesty, fairness, and transparency and not tolerate any forms of falsification, misrepresentation, or deception. Students are responsible for acting in accordance with the MedTech Honor Code, which covers both academic and non-academic misconduct. Academic violations are acts committed by a student, which interfere in any way with the fair and honest evaluation of his/her academic performance. Academic violations of the MedTech Honor Code include but are not limited to the following: ▪ Plagiarism of ideas or words. ▪ Any form of cheating. ▪ Presenting falsified research data. ▪ Submitting the same assignment in more than one course, without the consent of the instructor. Academic Year and Class Schedules The academic year at MedTech consists of two terms: Fall (from September to December) and Spring (from January to May), and an optional summer term (from end May to end June). Each term stretches over 15 weeks (about 3 and a half months) except the summer session which stretches over four weeks only. Class meeting times are typically scheduled Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. Make-up classes may be scheduled on Saturdays, with at least a week’s notice from the professor or the administration. section: VIII. Academic Integrity and Code of Conduct
text: VIII. Academic Integrity and Code of Conduct 1. Integrity MedTech places a strong emphasis on the integrity of academic work. It is the responsibility of all MedTech community members, including faculty, staff, and students, to conduct all academic endeavors with honesty, fairness, and transparency and not tolerate any forms of falsification, misrepresentation, or deception. Students are responsible for acting in accordance with the MedTech Honor Code, which covers both academic and non-academic misconduct. Academic violations are acts committed by a student, which interfere in any way with the fair and honest evaluation of his/her academic performance. Academic violations of the MedTech Honor Code include but are not limited to the following: ▪ Plagiarism of ideas or words. ▪ Any form of cheating. ▪ Presenting falsified research data. ▪ Submitting the same assignment in more than one course, without the consent of the instructor. Non-academic violations involve any type of non-academic misconduct. Non-academic violations of the MedTech Honor Code include but are not limited to the following: ▪ Destruction of school equipment or property. ▪ Disruption of the classroom. ▪ Use of unauthorized electronic equipment in the classroom. ▪ Verbal or physical abuse. ▪ Harassment. 2.
